e: Six people, including businessman Wicknell Chivayo, are killed in a helicopter crash in Marondera.
At least 27 people are killed near Chivhu when a minibus carrying church members to a conference collides head-on with a haulage truck.
A nationwide power blackout occurs after a technical fault on the national electricity grid of the state-owned utility ZESA.

The National Assembly passes a constitutional amendment extending presidential and parliamentary terms from five to seven years, and replacing direct presidential elections with selection by Parliament.
A freight train collides with a bus at a railway crossing in Triangle, killing nine people and injuring 25.
A minibus carrying schoolchildren catches fire in Gweru, killing seven passengers.
Zimbabwe is elected to a rotating seat at the United Nations Security Council.
A bus collides with a truck near Kwekwe, killing 10 people.
A bus crashes near Suswe, killing 10 people and injuring 45 others.
A minibus catches fire near Bulawayo, killing 18 people.
The government grants amnesty to 4,305 prisoners.
The government suspends exports of raw minerals and lithium concentrate.
Health authorities begin rolling out lenacapavir – a long-acting HIV prevention drug – targeting over 46,000 high-risk individuals across 24 sites.
